issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Rideable.messageOnRide() to have no parameters and return a String (calls in Main use r.messageOnRide()), but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement a version that requires an int parameter). This parameter mismatch is structural and will confuse students: the template and spec show a no-arg method, while the solution uses a different signature that cannot be called from the template's example code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/template by changing the Rideable interface and its implementations to use the no-argument signature: String messageOnRide(). Update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if a speed parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template (including example calls in Main and the UML) to specify and use messageOnRide(int speed).

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() : String on the Rideable interface (and calls it with no arguments in Main), but the solution implements Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and corresponding implementations in Pig and Seal. This signature mismatch changes the same conceptual operation (requesting the ride message) into a different API requiring an integer parameter and a different return format, creating confusion and a compile/runtime mismatch for students following the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent with the problem/template by using a no-argument method signature: String messageOnRide(). Update the solution's Rideable.java to declare messageOnRide() with no parameters and adjust Pig and Seal implementations to return the expected format (e.g., "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Alternatively, if the intention is to include speed, update the problem statement and template (Main) to document and call messageOnRide(int speed) consistently.
